card.name: Thidambu Nritham
card.tagline: Kerala temple dance carrying the deity's image on the head
card.profile: Thidambu Nritham is a Hindu temple ritual dance of North Malabar and Kasaragod district, Kerala, in which the dancer carries the 'thidambu' - the decorated image or replica of the deity, built on a bamboo frame - aloft on his head while performing rhythmic footwork to chenda drumming (Wikipedia; Kerala Tourism). It is performed mainly by Namboothiri Brahmins (occasionally by other Brahmin communities), is believed to be six to seven centuries old, and follows Natyashastra principles (Wikipedia). The performer wears a pleated skirt, silk vest, ornaments and a decorated turban; a full staging involves about ten people, including seven musicians and two lamp-bearers, and is associated with annual temple festivals, notably in Kannur (Kerala Tourism).
card.insight: The dance fuses devotion and discipline: balancing the heavy deity-image on the head while dancing transforms the performer into a living vehicle of the divine, and it is staged as part of temple festivals across North Malabar (Kerala Tourism; academic study, Neliti).
